findings.title: Revoke local recovery codes when replacing them in user storage
findings.body: For a federated user who already has recovery codes stored in Keycloak—the creation path used before this change—a successful external update leaves the existing local recovery credential untouched. Credential validation can still fall back to that local credential when the external validator rejects an input, so regenerating recovery codes does not invalidate the old set. Remove the previous local recovery credential when the external replacement succeeds, and test replacing an existing local set with a user-storage set.

findings.title: Remove exhausted credentials through the appropriate storage API
findings.body: The credential fetched here can now belong to external user storage, but the allCodesUsed() branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById(), which removes Keycloak-stored credentials rather than invoking the external CredentialInputUpdater. For a provider that retains exhausted credentials until disabled, this deletion does nothing. If the user abandons the subsequent reconfiguration action, the exhausted credential can remain configured, and the next recovery login fails when RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get(). Route exhausted external credentials through the user-storage disable/removal operation.

findings.title: Test recovery-code consumption rather than indefinitely reusable codes
findings.body: The new recovery validator accepts a matching code without consuming it, and getCredentials() reconstructs a completely unused credential from the original list on every read. Consequently, this fixture keeps requesting code 0 and accepts the same code indefinitely. The added integration test performs only one login, so it cannot detect broken advancement, replay rejection, or exhaustion handling in the newly supported federated path. Persist consumption state in the fixture and extend the test to reject reuse and exercise the last-code/reconfiguration path.
